title: Prefill gatekeeper routing: metrics contract, acceptance thresholds, and graceful fallback proposition
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Goal: Define a lightweight, operationally-safe prefill gatekeeper router that can route requests to cheap fast-path prefill variants and make an early acceptance decision with a clear metrics contract. The router must expose deterministic acceptance signals, be kernel-aware (so it picks model variants that map to compatible kernels and attention code paths), and specify an unambiguous fallback for degraded or mispredicted acceptance.

Motivation: Current speculative-prefill experiments suffer from noisy acceptance heuristics and unclear operational signals, which leads to undiagnosed increases in hallucination rates or hidden latency regressions. This ticket specifies the routing/acceptance contract, telemetry to evaluate decisions, and a fallback/playbook that on-call and SRE can follow during incidents or rollouts.
acceptance_criteria: Router chooses a prefill candidate variant and emits an acceptance signal within 10ms of receiving token stream metadata for >99% of requests in bench harness.
Early-accept decisions maintain 95th-percentile end-to-end token latency within target SLO (e2e_token_p95 <= 120ms) for canary traffic compared to baseline full-decode path.

Quality regression: automated sampling + eval suite shows no more than 0.5% delta in top-level intent-preservation metrics and <=1% delta in n-gram overlap for 95% of prompt families after enabling gatekeeper routing on a 1% canary.

Telemetry emitted for every routed request (see telemetry_plan) and dashboard updated; at rollout time the circuit breaker should be able to auto-trip if error-rate or hallucination proxy exceeds configured thresholds.
Fallback engages deterministically when acceptance signal is negative, probe times out, model variant kernel mismatch detected, or cost budget per request exceeds configured cap.
Runbook and automated rollback are verified on staging with injected acceptance failures and kernel-mismatch scenarios.
design_decisions: Use a two-stage admission: (1) candidate selection based on model variant/prefill-profile and kernel fingerprint, (2) fast acceptance scoring based on prefix-score delta and trusted confidence features.
Model variants: primary prefill = quantized-medium variant (faster kernels, lower KV memory); fallback = full precision standard decode variant.
Kernel awareness: router maintains a small fingerprint registry mapping model-version -> preferred kernel set. If preferred kernel unavailable on chosen host, route to fallback path conservatively.

Acceptance signal semantics: three-valued (ACCEPT / REJECT / TIMEOUT). ACCEPT commits speculative tokens; REJECT or TIMEOUT triggers immediate fallback to synchronous decode and cancels speculative commit.
Cost-aware guardrails: estimate per-request token-cost delta and refuse speculative prefill if expected cost grows beyond per-request cap (configurable via route-level policy).
telemetry_plan: Emit event: prefill.router.select {request_id, model_variant, kernel_fingerprint, time_ms}.
Emit event: prefill.router.acceptance {request_id, decision, score, probe_latency_ms, tokens_prefilled, fallback_reason?}.
Histogram: prefill_acceptance_score with custom buckets [-inf..0..inf] to capture distribution of acceptance scores.
Counter: prefill.fallback.count tagged by reason (kernel_mismatch, timeout, low_score, cost_overcap, runtime_error).
Latency metrics: prefill.probe_latency_p50/p95/p99 and end_to_end_token_latency_{baseline,prefill} for side-by-side comparison.
Quality sampling: 1% of ACCEPTs and 100% of REJECTs route to offline eval harness; results written to eval.s3 for automated checks.
Dashboard: top-level funnel showing candidate_select_rate -> acceptance_rate -> fallback_rate, plus per-model and per-kernel breakdowns.
rollout_plan: Stage 0 (lab): unit and integration tests; synthetic traffic with kernel-availability permutations.
Stage 1 (staging): enable on staging cluster with 100% synthetic traffic; inject kernel-mismatch and timeouts and validate fallback correctness.

Stage 2 (canary): 1% production traffic for 48 hours; monitor acceptance_score distribution and intent-preservation evals. Auto-roll back if any of the following breach: fallback_rate > 5%, hallucination_proxy_delta > 1.0%, e2e_token_p95 regression > 20%.
Stage 3 (gradual): increment traffic 5% -> 25% -> 50% over multiple cycles if metrics stable for 72h at each step.
Gate: toggle on/off via runtime flag per-tenant and per-region.
test_plan: Unit tests: scoring function determinism, kernel_registry lookups, decision timeouts.
Integration: simulated multi-host router with mixed kernel footprints, verify deterministic fallback and no duplicate commits.
Benchmarks: microbench prefill latency vs baseline using 3 sequence-length profiles (short, mid, long); measure p50/p95 token latency and cost-per-token delta.
A/B: shadow routing for 100k real requests; compare eval metrics and resource consumption before allowing speculative commit.
Chaos tests: kill kernel process after prefill select to ensure fallback path gracefully handles mid-flight migration.
fallback_playbook: If acceptance_signal == REJECT or TIMEOUT: cancel speculative KV commits, switch request to synchronous decode variant, mark request with fallback_reason and emit prefill.router.acceptance with decision=REJECT.
If kernel_mismatch detected on host: route to fallback host with compatibility tag; if not available, escalate to synchronous decode and increment kernel_mismatch counter.
Circuit breaker: if fallback_rate exceeds threshold for route (default 5% over 15m) auto-disable speculative prefill for that route and notify SRE/owner.
Operational steps: (1) gather prefill.* telemetry for last 15m, (2) run offline eval on sampled ACCEPTs, (3) if quality regressions present, rollback flag and open postmortem.
